pattern_title: VA acute leukemia inpatient outlier in TANF Standard
pattern_description: A single inpatient acute leukemia case is driving the VA increase in TANF Standard acute hospital spend. The pattern is highly concentrated and looks like a rare catastrophic case rather than broad utilization growth. Because the clinical and operational views point to the same event, the right action is a case-level review of coding, medical necessity, and reimbursement together.

individual_policies.policy_title: Flow Cytometry Policy, Professional and Facility
individual_policies.evidence: This policy addresses flow cytometry immunophenotyping and related cell enumeration rules for specific CPT/HCPCS codes and conditions. It does not mention CPT C9201 or any DRG acute leukemia inpatient outlier rule, so no adjudication rule is extracted for that pattern.

claims.summary: One VA TANF Standard acute hospital case added about $1.9M. Paid per admit increased by about $1.9M with 1 additional claim. Acute Leukemia with MCC drove nearly all of the positive change in this slice. Diagnosis C9201 appeared with no recorded procedure detail in the clinical view.

pattern_title: NJ rare IP Med/Surg case cluster
pattern_description: NJ shows a narrow IP Med/Surg cost increase tied to low-volume K5650 cases rather than a broad inpatient trend. The impact is concentrated in Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC and appears to reflect a small cluster of higher-cost cases. This should be handled as targeted clinical validation, not a broad utilization intervention.

claims.summary: NJ K5650 IP Med/Surg cases added about $50K across 3 claims. Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC was the main driver. Average paid per claim increased by about $17K. Procedure detail was blank in the clinical view.

pattern_title: NJ Family Care acute hospital payment spike
pattern_description: Within NJ Family Care, acute hospital spend rose from a very small base and was concentrated in a single higher-cost case. The pattern reflects both claim growth and higher paid amount per case, but it is not broad enough to indicate a market-wide hospital trend. The business lever is claim-level reimbursement and admission review.

claims.summary: One NJ Family Care acute hospital claim added about $30K. Paid per admit increased by about $30K with 1 additional claim. This single case represented just over half of the positive change in the operational slice.

pattern_title: AR MINIMED DME mapping issue across clinical and LTSS views
pattern_description: AR shows a small but recurring provider-specific signal tied to MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP, with activity appearing in both OP HH/DME and LTSS Non Dual views. The common issue is classification quality: facility and clinical fields are not mapped cleanly enough to support confident utilization or reimbursement action. This is a gating validation pattern first, with provider follow-up only after mapping is corrected.
